news.title: Six questions facing England as they target next year’s Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Starting positions at centre-back and No 10 are up for grabs, while Sarina Wiegman’s future continues to be in the air. England have two jobs to do on Tuesday. The first, avoiding an almighty upset and progressing past Greece on aggregate in their Women’s World Cup playoff to reach a final tie, should be a formality for one of the world’s best-resourced teams. The second, honing their style to play like contenders for next summer’s World Cup in Brazil, is a far trickier but crucial challenge.

news.title: Argentina were World Cup’s most targeted team online, says FIFA report
news.lede: Argentina were the most targeted national team on social media during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with accusations of referee favouritism, corruption and xenophobia among the main forms of abuse directed at the side, a FIFA report published on October 9 noted. The governing body’s Social Media Protection Service (SMPS) analysed more than 17.1 million posts and comments on X, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok between June 9 and July 20. Of those, 477,000 were referred for human review, with 240,000 verified as abusive. England were the second-most targeted team, followed by Spain, Brazil and Norway, the report found.

news.title: Football fans can drink alcohol in seats during Scotland game
news.lede: Renfrewshire Council has granted a licence for the controlled sale of alcohol at the second leg of Scotland’s encounter with Czechia. Football fans will be able to drink alcohol in the stands in Scotland for the first time in more than four decades at Tuesday’s Women’s World Cup play-off. Renfrewshire Council has granted a licence for the controlled sale of alcohol at the second leg of Scotland’s encounter with Czechia at St Mirren’s Marbill Coaches Stadium in Paisley. Major restrictions on alcohol sales were introduced after Rangers and Celtic fans clashed on the Hampden pitch after the 1980 Scottish Cup final.

news.title: Chris Wilder can still strike Sheffield United transfer gold - we saw it at the World Cup
news.lede: Chris Wilder may yet have unearthed a valuable asset for Sheffield United in Tahith Chong, whose promising World Cup displays for Curacao offered a reminder of his ability. After an injury-disrupted start to life at Bramall Lane, the versatile winger or attacking midfielder finally made his mark by scoring in the Blades' 3-0 win over Lincoln City. Patrick Bamford's brace either side of Chong's goal collected their third league win of the season. With creativity in short supply for Chris Wilder's Sheffield United side, could this be the beginning of a long-awaited breakthrough for Chong?

news.title: 2026 FIFA World Cup Winner Hails Osimhen Ahead of Champions League Clash Barcelona
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Find it fast with our new search feature at Legit.ng! Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsi has described Victor Osimhen as one of the best strikers in the world, issuing the warning ahead of his side's 2026/27 UEFA Champions League group stage visit to Galatasaray's Rams Park in Istanbul on matchday two. The Spanish defender recalled a previous encounter with the Super Eagles star, when Osimhen was still leading the line for Napoli in 2024. Drawing on that experience, Cubarsi said Barcelona know what to expect from the Nigerian forward, particularly in a home setting where the Turkish side will be backing their striker heavily.
